It differs from standard training by explicitly decoupling the learning of general scene structure from the refinement of density bias and object compactness [S1, S2].

The claim states that the method differs from standard training by explicitly decoupling the learning of general scene structure from the refinement of density bias and object compactness. Source [S1] supports the part about decoupling general scene structure from density bias (by applying density prior only after step 100 to ensure the general scene is well-represented). However, Source [S2] discusses using sparsity loss to encourage compact object generation and background augmentation to eliminate artifacts, but it does not explicitly describe a 'decoupling' of learning general scene structure from object compactness in the same manner as S1 describes for density bias. Furthermore, the claim combines 'density bias' (from S1) and 'object compactness' (from S2) into a single decoupling mechanism, which is not explicitly stated as a unified strategy in the provided texts. S1 focuses on density prior timing, and S2 focuses on sparsity loss and background augmentation for artifact removal. While both papers address aspects of the claim, the specific phrasing of 'explicitly decoupling... from... object compactness' is not fully supported by S2, which treats sparsity loss as a regularization term rather than a decoupled phase of learning general structure. Therefore, only part of the claim is fully supported.
